$comment: The motion registry (ADR-0024 §3): the ONLY place an animation may be declared. tools/gen_ui.py validates it and generates src/state/motion.ts; tests/v1/design and test/motion.test.ts gate the source against it. Values are the approved ones of ADR-0024 §6, rulebook §21 (A-01..A-17) and design system §8, never invented. status 'built' = the code runs it (and must be bound: a keyframe, a transition selector or a Loop.animate id); 'approved' = decided, not built yet, and the build fails if code uses it before the entry says 'built'. Instant or static affordances that never animate (selection, focus, the loading skeleton, the graph layout) are not motions and have no entry; the halo has one because ADR-0024 names it with its idle rule. max_ms null = static (draws once, never animates). cap null = no cap; cap_per says what it counts (the whole surface, or one target). over_cap is given only where a source states the policy; absent, the conservative default holds: a start at the cap is refused. replay is false for every entry: nothing replays after a re-read, resync or reconnect (ADR-0024 §5).

state-change.trigger: a row's domain state differs from the one it last rendered (never on first appearance)
state-change.reduced: instant: the new glyph and word appear at once
state-change.equivalent: the state glyph and its word

inspector-open.reduced: instant: the inspector is there at once

sheet-open.trigger: the user opens the inspector on a phone (a bottom sheet)
sheet-open.reduced: instant: the sheet is there at once

dialog-open.reduced: instant: the dialog is there at once

pointer-affordance.equivalent: the focus ring and the control's own label

camera-settle.trigger: the user moves the graph camera (focus, search, zoom, fit)
camera-settle.reduced: jump: the camera is at its target in one frame
camera-settle.equivalent: the focus is announced and its mirror row is selected

execution-pulse.trigger: an execution.* frame about a loaded execution whose edge is live
execution-pulse.reduced: removed: the live edge is drawn thicker and static instead
execution-pulse.equivalent: the execution's state word (Running) in the mirror and the Relations list

row-pulse.trigger: an execution.* frame whose execution, read again from Core, is live and belongs to a mission whose row is on screen: one opacity step on that row
row-pulse.reduced: removed (and while frames run slow): the event still counts as presented, so it never plays later
row-pulse.equivalent: the mission's state word on the row (Core records no last-output time, so no 'output N s ago')

activity-halo.source: ADR-0024 §5-6, rulebook §21 A-03, P18 A8 as amended, ADR-0028 §3
activity-halo.trigger: a read of Core's state shows the object's presentation class active; it clears only when a read shows it is not (hysteresis: the view draws the last read it holds, which survives a lost stream, a resync and a failed re-read)
activity-halo.reduced: kept: it is static, so reduced motion shows the same halo
activity-halo.equivalent: the node's state word in the graph mirror, and 'live work now' beside it

travelling-marker.source: ADR-0024 §6, rulebook §21 A-04, ADR-0030 (amends P18 A8)
travelling-marker.trigger: an execution.* frame whose subject is a loaded execution with a drawn live executions.task_id edge (Core's recorded relation): one marker per frame, i.e. per output batch, from the execution's end to the task's end
travelling-marker.reduced: removed: the live edge is drawn 2 px and static; the event still counts as presented, so it never plays later
travelling-marker.equivalent: the mirror says the edge is live: 'live now' on the execution's attempt-of relation

thread-travel.source: ADR-0024 §6, ADR-0026 §1, rulebook §21 A-05, design system §2
thread-travel.trigger: a new Archeus message whose links[] target a row on screen: one line from the message to that row, drawn on once and gone; built on Now, and on the mission Now tab with P19's per-mission conversations
thread-travel.reduced: no line: the row and the message's card keep their change rule (T2) while the digest names the object
thread-travel.equivalent: a polite announcement 'Archeus updated …' naming the objects, and the message's card or link

thread-rule-fade.reduced: instant: the rule is gone at once
thread-rule-fade.equivalent: the row is no longer marked as changed

presence-orbit.trigger: a batch of execution.* frames: the mark's node goes once round its orbit and parks where it started
presence-orbit.reduced: colour only: the node shows the presence and no turn is drawn; the event still counts as presented
presence-orbit.equivalent: the operations strip's counts, said in a status region at most once per 30 s

attention-arrival.trigger: the attention count increased: a read of /v1/attention at a newer Core seq than the one held shows a higher count (the first read sets the baseline and never pulses; a fall is not an arrival)
attention-arrival.equivalent: the new count announced politely, the badge's own count and its label, and the count in the tab's name

toast.trigger: work that ran at least 10 s finished while its row was not on screen (D-8): an execution.ended frame whose attempt Core reads as ENDED_OK, its own started_at and ended_at 10 s or more apart, with no row or inspector of its mission or attempt on screen
toast.reduced: no fade: the toast appears and leaves at once
toast.equivalent: its text in a role=status region mounted at boot; never the only signal — the mission's row and state changed too

activity-chip.trigger: an execution.hook frame whose execution, read again from Core, holds a current action newer than the last one chipped and belongs to a mission whose row is on screen: one chip on that row (ttl_error_ms when Core refused or held the call)
activity-chip.reduced: no fade: the chip appears and leaves at once
activity-chip.equivalent: the chip's text; a refused or held chip is also announced beside its row's link
